I have an idea for another page... a shared / collaborative slot machine 
let me explain 
It is very similar to the existing board 
except instead of posting text yourself, 
the message is a random five letter string A-Z0-9
there is a big button you can press and when you do, 
the slot machine animation starts 
the server decides on a random string 
if any three or more characters are the same 
you are a "winner" 
if all five are in ascending or descending order 
you are a "winner" 
you can't press the button until the animation has settled fully 
nobody can press the button until the animation has settled fully 
then the next person who presses it goes next 
but nobody knows who pressed 
there is no sign in or any name associated with any press
but you know if your button press worked 
or not 
all we care about is the messages 
same as before 
we store all previous messages locally 
same island idea as before 
same reconciliation idea as before 
the animation should be beautiful like a slot machine 
but remember no money changes hands, this is all for fun 
once you have successfully pressed the button ten times 
you get a second button 
this second button means you no longer have to press the button manually 
it automatically retries to press the button once the animation has settled 
in the results, 
unlike before, 
we need some kind of visual indication for "winners" 
and we also need to explain in the about page what the "winners" are 
and what the technical aspects of this page are

If only a few files (under five or there about) need to change, give me the full path of the files that need to change and the FULL file 
if there are a lot of files that need to change 
    Delivery
    Whole project as one tar.gz, unambiguous file placement
    Any files to delete on updates called out explicitly
    No bespoke sed/patch scripts — full files only for anything that changes
    Docs updated alongside code changes
    Low verbosity, no code comments

That touches 37 files, so here’s the whole project as one archive: chaos-velixir-run-slots.tar.gz. Paths are relative to the repo root:

cd ~/src/dotnet/chaos-velixir-run
tar -xzf ~/Downloads/chaos-velixir-run-slots.tar.gz
bash scripts/run-all.sh
Files to delete: none. The archive leaves out LICENSE and tests/js/package-lock.json because they weren’t in your dump. Your copies stay as they are.

How it works

Server (Slots/SlotService.cs): a press draws five symbols with RandomNumberGenerator. It then refuses every press until SpinMilliseconds (4 s by default) has passed. A press made during a spin is refused before the per-client rate limit, so waiting doesn’t cost you anything.
Same model as the board: results are UUIDv7 messages, the server keeps the newest 50, and the offer/merge/delta logic is shared. That merge logic now lives in Messages/MessageWindow.cs, and BoardService uses it too.
Late joiners: they get spin: { id, remaining } and animate only the time that’s left. Each browser plays its reels for the remaining time from when it receives the spin. Since that’s always later than the server’s clock, your button can’t come back on before the server lock has ended.
What you see after pressing: “Your press worked” or “Someone else pressed first”. Your own results get a “Your press” tag, which only your browser knows about.
Winners:
Three or more of the same symbol anywhere, or five strictly ascending or descending (digits sort before letters).
About 1 spin in 50 wins.
A winning spin gets a gold border, a ★ badge, highlighted symbols, flashing lights and a gold payline.
Auto spin:
Appears after 10 successful presses, counted in localStorage.
It presses 200–1000 ms after each settle, so it doesn’t always beat everyone else.
It pauses while the tab is hidden and is off on every page load.
Reels: each reel moves with the Web Animations API, with a wind-up, motion blur, an overshoot and a thunk as it stops. With reduced motion turned on, the symbols just change. The CSP is unchanged because there are no inline styles.
About page: now has a Slots section, a Winners section and the technical details. “Clear local history” now clears both databases and the press count.
Unrelated fix: your failing canvas E2E test was most likely a race. Playwright could start drawing before the first snapshot arrived, and the canvas ignores input until then. The canvas now sets data-ready once that snapshot arrives, and the test waits for it.

Testing: I couldn’t build the .NET code here because there’s no SDK in my sandbox. The JS tests pass (51, including 19 new ones). I also ran a full client simulation against a fake server, covering pressing, landing, the “mine” tag, auto spin, a reload and joining mid-spin, and it all worked. If the strict analyzers object to anything, send me the output.


Chaos velixir run slots.tar
GZ

Ran a command
The compiler can’t tell that text is non-null in Hits, because the earlier Classify(text) call doesn’t carry the [NotNullWhen] guarantee back to the caller. The fix is to check IsValid(text) directly at the start of Hits.

Only one file changes. The test projects build after Chaos.Web, so they haven’t been compiled yet. If they report anything, send it over.

The execute bits were my fault: I rebuilt the files from the dump, which dropped the permissions, so the archive shipped the scripts without +x. Since you’ve already run chmod, nothing else is needed, and future archives will keep the bit.

src/Chaos.Web/Slots/SlotRules.cs

csharp
using System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis;
using System.Security.Cryptography;

namespace Chaos.Web.Slots;

internal static class SlotRules
{
    public const int Length = 5;
    public const string Symbols = "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ";

    public static string Draw() => RandomNumberGenerator.GetString(Symbols, Length);

    public static bool IsValid([NotNullWhen(true)] string? text)
    {
        if (text is null || text.Length != Length)
        {
            return false;
        }

        foreach (var c in text)
        {
            if (!char.IsAsciiDigit(c) && !char.IsAsciiLetterUpper(c))
            {
                return false;
            }
        }

        return true;
    }

    public static SlotWin Classify(string? text)
    {
        if (!IsValid(text))
        {
            return SlotWin.None;
        }

        var most = text.GroupBy(c => c).Max(group => group.Count());
        if (most >= 5)
        {
            return SlotWin.FiveOfAKind;
        }

        if (most == 4)
        {
            return SlotWin.FourOfAKind;
        }

        if (most == 3)
        {
            return SlotWin.ThreeOfAKind;
        }

        if (IsOrdered(text, 1))
        {
            return SlotWin.StraightUp;
        }

        return IsOrdered(text, -1) ? SlotWin.StraightDown : SlotWin.None;
    }

    public static bool[] Hits(string? text)
    {
        var hits = new bool[Length];
        if (!IsValid(text))
        {
            return hits;
        }

        var win = Classify(text);
        if (win is SlotWin.None)
        {
            return hits;
        }

        if (win is SlotWin.StraightUp or SlotWin.StraightDown)
        {
            Array.Fill(hits, true);
            return hits;
        }

        var top = text.GroupBy(c => c).MaxBy(group => group.Count())!.Key;
        for (var i = 0; i < Length; i++)
        {
            hits[i] = text[i] == top;
        }

        return hits;
    }

    public static string Label(SlotWin win) => win switch
    {
        SlotWin.ThreeOfAKind => "Three of a kind",
        SlotWin.FourOfAKind => "Four of a kind",
        SlotWin.FiveOfAKind => "Five of a kind",
        SlotWin.StraightUp => "Straight up",
        SlotWin.StraightDown => "Straight down",
        _ => "",
    };

    public static char Above(char symbol) => Symbols[(Symbols.IndexOf(symbol, StringComparison.Ordinal) + 1) % Symbols.Length];

    public static char Below(char symbol) => Symbols[(Symbols.IndexOf(symbol, StringComparison.Ordinal) + Symbols.Length - 1) % Symbols.Length];

    private static bool IsOrdered(string text, int direction)
    {
        for (var i = 1; i < text.Length; i++)
        {
            if ((text[i] - text[i - 1]) * direction <= 0)
            {
                return false;
            }
        }

        return true;
    }
}

The compiler can’t tell that text is non-null in Hits, because the earlier Classify(text) call doesn’t carry the [NotNullWhen] guarantee back to the caller. The fix is to check IsValid(text) directly at the start of Hits.

src/Chaos.Web/Slots/SlotRules.cs

csharp
using System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis;
using System.Security.Cryptography;

namespace Chaos.Web.Slots;

internal static class SlotRules
{
    public const int Length = 5;
    public const string Symbols = "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ";

    public static string Draw() => RandomNumberGenerator.GetString(Symbols, Length);

    public static bool IsValid([NotNullWhen(true)] string? text)
    {
        if (text is null || text.Length != Length)
        {
            return false;
        }

        foreach (var c in text)
        {
            if (!char.IsAsciiDigit(c) && !char.IsAsciiLetterUpper(c))
            {
                return false;
            }
        }

        return true;
    }

    public static SlotWin Classify(string? text)
    {
        if (!IsValid(text))
        {
            return SlotWin.None;
        }

        var most = text.GroupBy(c => c).Max(group => group.Count());
        if (most >= 5)
        {
            return SlotWin.FiveOfAKind;
        }

        if (most == 4)
        {
            return SlotWin.FourOfAKind;
        }

        if (most == 3)
        {
            return SlotWin.ThreeOfAKind;
        }

        if (IsOrdered(text, 1))
        {
            return SlotWin.StraightUp;
        }

        return IsOrdered(text, -1) ? SlotWin.StraightDown : SlotWin.None;
    }

    public static bool[] Hits(string? text)
    {
        var hits = new bool[Length];
        if (!IsValid(text))
        {
            return hits;
        }

        var win = Classify(text);
        if (win is SlotWin.None)
        {
            return hits;
        }

        if (win is SlotWin.StraightUp or SlotWin.StraightDown)
        {
            Array.Fill(hits, true);
            return hits;
        }

        var top = text.GroupBy(c => c).MaxBy(group => group.Count())!.Key;
        for (var i = 0; i < Length; i++)
        {
            hits[i] = text[i] == top;
        }

        return hits;
    }

    public static string Label(SlotWin win) => win switch
    {
        SlotWin.ThreeOfAKind => "Three of a kind",
        SlotWin.FourOfAKind => "Four of a kind",
        SlotWin.FiveOfAKind => "Five of a kind",
        SlotWin.StraightUp => "Straight up",
        SlotWin.StraightDown => "Straight down",
        _ => "",
    };

    public static char Above(char symbol) => Symbols[(Symbols.IndexOf(symbol, StringComparison.Ordinal) + 1) % Symbols.Length];

    public static char Below(char symbol) => Symbols[(Symbols.IndexOf(symbol, StringComparison.Ordinal) + Symbols.Length - 1) % Symbols.Length];

    private static bool IsOrdered(string text, int direction)
    {
        for (var i = 1; i < text.Length; i++)
        {
            if ((text[i] - text[i - 1]) * direction <= 0)
            {
                return false;
            }
        }

        return true;
    }
}

/work/tests/Chaos.E2E/bin/Release/net10.0/Chaos.E2E.dll (net10.0|x64) failed with 1 error(s) (18s 298ms)
Exit code: 2

Ran 4 commands
The canvas never got its first snapshot, and this was also the cause of the original 30-second canvas failure. The readiness check I added only made it fail sooner.

The canvas script asks the server to start sending updates (Join) during attach, before attach has returned to .NET. The server queued the snapshot right away, but at that moment it didn’t yet have the handle to the browser script. The send failed and the update channel stopped, so nothing arrived until the 25-second ping re-joined.

The board and slots didn’t hit this only because they read local history before joining, which gives attach time to return.

The fix is on the server: each island now waits until its script is attached before sending anything. All three islands get it so the next new island doesn’t repeat the problem.

src/Chaos.Web/Components/Islands/CanvasIsland.razor

razor
@implements IAsyncDisposable
@inject CanvasService Canvas
@inject IJSRuntime JS
@inject ILogger<CanvasIsland> Logger

<div class="stage">
    <canvas @ref="_canvas" class="paper" width="1024" height="1024" role="img"
            aria-label="Shared drawing canvas. Drawing needs a mouse, a finger or a stylus."></canvas>
</div>
<div class="tools">
    <button type="button" @onclick="Reset" disabled="@(!_ready)">Reset canvas</button>
    <output class="status">@_status</output>
</div>

@code {
    private ElementReference _canvas;
    private readonly TaskCompletionSource _attached = new(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously);
    private DotNetObjectReference<CanvasIsland>? _self;
    private IJSObjectReference? _module;
    private IJSObjectReference? _client;
    private Outbox<CanvasUpdate>? _outbox;
    private Subscriber? _subscriber;
    private CanvasSession? _session;
    private string? _status;
    private bool _ready;

    [Parameter, EditorRequired]
    public string Client { get; set; } = ClientAddress.Unknown;

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (!firstRender)
        {
            return;
        }

        _self = DotNetObjectReference.Create(this);
        _module = await JS.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("import", ModulePath.Of(Assets["Components/Islands/CanvasIsland.razor.js"]));
        _client = await _module.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("attach", _canvas, _self);
        _attached.TrySetResult();
        _ready = true;
        StateHasChanged();
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public async Task Join()
    {
        await StopAsync();
        var outbox = new Outbox<CanvasUpdate>(256, 64, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(20), SendAsync, Logger);
        _outbox = outbox;
        _subscriber = new Subscriber(outbox);
        _session = Canvas.OpenSession(_subscriber);
        Canvas.Subscribe(_subscriber);
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public int Draw(int stroke, int epoch, int[] points, bool end)
    {
        if (_session is null || points is null)
        {
            return (int)DrawResult.Invalid;
        }

        var result = Canvas.Draw(_session, epoch, stroke, points, end);
        SetStatus(result switch
        {
            DrawResult.TooFast => "Slow down a little.",
            DrawResult.Full => "The canvas is full. Reset it to keep drawing.",
            DrawResult.TooLong => "That stroke got too long, so it ended.",
            _ => null,
        });
        return (int)result;
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public bool Ping() => _subscriber is not null && _outbox is { IsFaulted: false } && Canvas.IsSubscribed(_subscriber);

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
    {
        await StopAsync();
        await JsCleanup.DisposeAsync(_client, "dispose");
        await JsCleanup.DisposeAsync(_module, null);
        _self?.Dispose();
    }

    private void Reset()
    {
        _status = Canvas.Reset(Client) is ResetResult.TooFast ? "It was just reset. Try again in a second." : null;
    }

    private void SetStatus(string? status)
    {
        if (status != _status)
        {
            _status = status;
            StateHasChanged();
        }
    }

    private async Task SendAsync(IReadOnlyList<CanvasUpdate> batch, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await _attached.Task.WaitAsync(cancellationToken);
        await InvokeAsync(() => _client is null
            ? Task.FromException(new InvalidOperationException("The canvas module is not attached."))
            : _client.InvokeVoidAsync("apply", cancellationToken, batch).AsTask());
    }

    private async Task StopAsync()
    {
        if (_session is not null)
        {
            Canvas.Abandon(_session);
            _session = null;
        }

        if (_subscriber is not null)
        {
            Canvas.Unsubscribe(_subscriber);
            _subscriber = null;
        }

        if (_outbox is not null)
        {
            await _outbox.DisposeAsync();
            _outbox = null;
        }
    }

    private sealed class Subscriber(Outbox<CanvasUpdate> outbox) : ICanvasSubscriber
    {
        public bool Deliver(CanvasUpdate update) => outbox.TryPost(update);
    }
}
src/Chaos.Web/Components/Islands/BoardIsland.razor

razor
@implements IAsyncDisposable
@inject BoardService Board
@inject IJSRuntime JS
@inject ILogger<BoardIsland> Logger

<form class="compose" @onsubmit="Send">
    <label class="visually-hidden" for="compose-text">Message</label>
    <textarea id="compose-text" @bind="_draft" maxlength="@MessageText.MaxLength" rows="3" required
              placeholder="Write something everyone here will see" disabled="@(!_ready)"></textarea>
    <div class="actions">
        <output class="status" for="compose-text">@_status</output>
        <span class="hint">Ctrl+Enter sends</span>
        <button type="submit" disabled="@(!_ready)">Send</button>
    </div>
</form>

@code {
    private readonly TaskCompletionSource _attached = new(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously);
    private DotNetObjectReference<BoardIsland>? _self;
    private IJSObjectReference? _module;
    private IJSObjectReference? _client;
    private Outbox<BoardUpdate>? _outbox;
    private Subscriber? _subscriber;
    private string? _draft;
    private string? _status;
    private bool _ready;
    private int _offered;

    [Parameter, EditorRequired]
    public string Client { get; set; } = ClientAddress.Unknown;

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (!firstRender)
        {
            return;
        }

        _self = DotNetObjectReference.Create(this);
        _module = await JS.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("import", ModulePath.Of(Assets["Components/Islands/BoardIsland.razor.js"]));
        _client = await _module.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("attach", _self);
        _attached.TrySetResult();
        _ready = true;
        StateHasChanged();
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public int Offer(string[] ids, string[] texts)
    {
        if (ids is null || texts is null || ids.Length != texts.Length)
        {
            return 0;
        }

        var count = Math.Min(BoardService.MaxOffers - _offered, ids.Length);
        if (count <= 0)
        {
            return 0;
        }

        _offered += count;
        var offered = new List<BoardMessage>(count);
        for (var i = 0; i < count; i++)
        {
            if (Guid.TryParseExact(ids[i], "D", out var id) && texts[i] is { } text)
            {
                offered.Add(new BoardMessage(id, text));
            }
        }

        return Board.Offer(offered);
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public async Task Join()
    {
        await StopAsync();
        var outbox = new Outbox<BoardUpdate>(64, 16, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(20), SendAsync, Logger);
        _outbox = outbox;
        _subscriber = new Subscriber(outbox);
        Board.Subscribe(_subscriber);
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public bool Ping() => _subscriber is not null && _outbox is { IsFaulted: false } && Board.IsSubscribed(_subscriber);

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
    {
        await StopAsync();
        await JsCleanup.DisposeAsync(_client, "dispose");
        await JsCleanup.DisposeAsync(_module, null);
        _self?.Dispose();
    }

    private void Send()
    {
        var result = Board.Post(_draft, Client);
        _status = result switch
        {
            PostResult.Empty => "Type a message first.",
            PostResult.TooFast => "Slow down. You can post again in a moment.",
            PostResult.Repeat => "That message was just posted.",
            _ => null,
        };

        if (result is PostResult.Accepted)
        {
            _draft = null;
        }
    }

    private async Task SendAsync(IReadOnlyList<BoardUpdate> batch, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await _attached.Task.WaitAsync(cancellationToken);
        await InvokeAsync(() => _client is null
            ? Task.FromException(new InvalidOperationException("The board module is not attached."))
            : _client.InvokeVoidAsync("apply", cancellationToken, batch).AsTask());
    }

    private async Task StopAsync()
    {
        if (_subscriber is not null)
        {
            Board.Unsubscribe(_subscriber);
            _subscriber = null;
        }

        if (_outbox is not null)
        {
            await _outbox.DisposeAsync();
            _outbox = null;
        }
    }

    private sealed class Subscriber(Outbox<BoardUpdate> outbox) : IBoardSubscriber
    {
        public bool Deliver(BoardUpdate update) => outbox.TryPost(update);
    }
}

@implements IAsyncDisposable
@inject SlotService Slots
@inject IJSRuntime JS
@inject ILogger<SlotIsland> Logger

<section @ref="_machine" class="machine" aria-labelledby="machine-title" data-initial="@_face">
    <h2 id="machine-title" class="visually-hidden">Slot machine</h2>
    <div class="lights" aria-hidden="true">
        @for (var i = 0; i < Bulbs; i++)
        {
            <span></span>
        }
    </div>
    <div class="window" aria-hidden="true">
        @foreach (var symbol in _face)
        {
            <div class="reel"><div class="strip"><span>@SlotRules.Above(symbol)</span><span>@symbol</span><span>@SlotRules.Below(symbol)</span></div></div>
        }
        <div class="payline"></div>
    </div>
    <p class="verdict" aria-hidden="true"></p>
    <div class="controls">
        <button type="button" class="spin" disabled>Spin</button>
        <button type="button" class="auto" aria-pressed="false" hidden>Auto spin</button>
    </div>
    <output class="status"></output>
    <p class="progress"></p>
</section>

@code {
    private const int Bulbs = 18;

    private ElementReference _machine;
    private readonly TaskCompletionSource _attached = new(TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously);
    private DotNetObjectReference<SlotIsland>? _self;
    private IJSObjectReference? _module;
    private IJSObjectReference? _client;
    private Outbox<SlotUpdate>? _outbox;
    private Subscriber? _subscriber;
    private string _face = "CHAOS";
    private int _offered;

    [Parameter, EditorRequired]
    public string Client { get; set; } = ClientAddress.Unknown;

    [Parameter]
    public string? Face { get; set; }

    protected override void OnParametersSet() => _face = SlotRules.IsValid(Face) ? Face : "CHAOS";

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (!firstRender)
        {
            return;
        }

        _self = DotNetObjectReference.Create(this);
        _module = await JS.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("import", ModulePath.Of(Assets["Components/Islands/SlotIsland.razor.js"]));
        _client = await _module.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>("attach", _machine, _self);
        _attached.TrySetResult();
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public int Offer(string[] ids, string[] texts)
    {
        if (ids is null || texts is null || ids.Length != texts.Length)
        {
            return 0;
        }

        var count = Math.Min(SlotService.MaxOffers - _offered, ids.Length);
        if (count <= 0)
        {
            return 0;
        }

        _offered += count;
        var offered = new List<BoardMessage>(count);
        for (var i = 0; i < count; i++)
        {
            if (Guid.TryParseExact(ids[i], "D", out var id) && texts[i] is { } text)
            {
                offered.Add(new BoardMessage(id, text));
            }
        }

        return Slots.Offer(offered);
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public async Task Join()
    {
        await StopAsync();
        var outbox = new Outbox<SlotUpdate>(64, 16, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(20), SendAsync, Logger);
        _outbox = outbox;
        _subscriber = new Subscriber(outbox);
        Slots.Subscribe(_subscriber);
    }

    [JSInvokable]
    public string Press() => Slots.Press(Client).Reply;

    [JSInvokable]
    public bool Ping() => _subscriber is not null && _outbox is { IsFaulted: false } && Slots.IsSubscribed(_subscriber);

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
    {
        await StopAsync();
        await JsCleanup.DisposeAsync(_client, "dispose");
        await JsCleanup.DisposeAsync(_module, null);
        _self?.Dispose();
    }

    private async Task SendAsync(IReadOnlyList<SlotUpdate> batch, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        await _attached.Task.WaitAsync(cancellationToken);
        await InvokeAsync(() => _client is null
            ? Task.FromException(new InvalidOperationException("The slot module is not attached."))
            : _client.InvokeVoidAsync("apply", cancellationToken, batch).AsTask());
    }

    private async Task StopAsync()
    {
        if (_subscriber is not null)
        {
            Slots.Unsubscribe(_subscriber);
            _subscriber = null;
        }

        if (_outbox is not null)
        {
            await _outbox.DisposeAsync();
            _outbox = null;
        }
    }

    private sealed class Subscriber(Outbox<SlotUpdate> outbox) : ISlotSubscriber
    {
        public bool Deliver(SlotUpdate update) => outbox.TryPost(update);
    }

docs/adr/0007-realtime-delivery.md

markdown
# 0007 Per-client outboxes over the circuit

Status: accepted

- Transport is the Blazor circuit itself: JS calls `[JSInvokable]` methods, the server calls the module's `apply`. No separate SignalR hub and no extra JavaScript client.
- Each island owns a bounded channel (`Outbox<T>`) drained by one pump that sends batches in order and waits for the browser to finish each batch. A full outbox, a failed call or a 20 s stall drops the subscriber.
- The pump waits until the island's module has been attached. JavaScript can call `Join` before `attach` has returned to .NET, and an earlier send would fault the outbox.
- Subscribing enqueues a snapshot under the same lock as updates, so nothing is missed or duplicated.
- Board deltas carry `version` and `previous`; a gap triggers a fresh snapshot. Canvas updates carry an offset per stroke; a gap triggers a fresh snapshot.
- The browser pings every 25 s and resubscribes when the server says it was dropped, and resubscribes after every reconnect.



Claude is AI and can make mistakes. Please double-check responses.
